$comment: Limits for tests/middleware-e2e/perf.mjs. The gate fails when a measured value exceeds its limit.
Optimize p50 is gated as a ratio to a calibration request sent in the same round, so a slower host moves both sides.
The small optimize is dominated by its SQLite commit, so it is divided by a receipt (same HTTP, auth and queue path
plus one commit, no optimize work). The large optimize is CPU-bound, so it is divided by capabilities (HTTP and auth
only, no storage), which a slow CI disk cannot inflate.
Ratio limits: 3 x the median of the 5 `node tests/middleware-e2e/perf.mjs --measure` runs in `measured`, rounded up
to 2 significant digits. On that host the gate fails at a 3.0x rise of small/receipt (median 2.33, limit 7.0) and a
3.1x rise of large/capabilities (median 61.38, limit 190). A disk with slower fsync adds the same commit time to the
small optimize and the receipt, which lowers the small ratio: there the small gate needs a larger regression of the
optimize work to fail. The large gate has no storage in its baseline and keeps its threshold.
p99 is not gated as a ratio: it is the 2nd-3rd largest of 100-200 samples, and dividing two such tails swung 0.9-2.8
(small) and 18-51 (large) across runs. p99 gets an absolute ceiling, max(20 x the median of the 5 runs, 250 ms),
which catches a pathological tail (a lock wait, a stalled queue), not an fsync stall or a busy host.
The receipt p50 is not gated against capabilities: it pays one WAL fsync (synchronous=FULL) that costs 10-15 ms on
Linux CI disks against ~0.4 ms for capabilities. It gets an absolute 50 ms ceiling (~3x a slow CI fsync, ~77x the
local median 0.65 ms), so it catches only a pathological commit path.
Go benchmarks are CPU-bound absolute ns/op: 5 x the largest of 3 runs.
Re-derive after a deliberate performance change.

measured.host: Apple M3 Pro, darwin/arm64, go1.26.5, node 22.22.2 (shared with other workloads, load average 4-17)
measured.http_host: same host, load average 3.5-5.6; proxy binary built before the receipt Revoked-query change
